JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondent U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act for claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of Santhosh @ Lakanna S/o.Ramanna in a motor vehicle accident took place on 16012018.

2. The brief contents of petition is that:
On 16012018, at about 9.30 p.m., the deceased by name Santhosh @ Lakanna S/o.Ramanna had been to Hemagiri Fair, after attending the fair he was returned to his native Lakshmipura on motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA 04HB2586 along with pillion riders, when they reached near Kanthaiahna Palya on Huliyurdurga,
Amruthuru Main Road, at that time, the Indica Car bearing reg.No.KA 11A4472 from Amruthur to Huliyurdurga driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motorcycle, as a result, the rider and pillion riders fell down and sustained injury.

The injured were shifted to the Government hospital,
Kunigal, on the way to the hospital the rider by name Santhosh @ Lakkanna succumbed to the injuries.
The accident was occurred solely on the negligence of driver of the offending car.
The petitioners are the legal representative and dependents on the deceased.
The deceased was working as waterman in Gram Panchayath and also doing welding work and earning of Rs.20,000/p.m.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earner.
3. Further the contention of the petitioners is that, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna.
4. The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the driver ofthe offending Indica car bearing reg.No.KA11A4472.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

5. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their respective counsel, the respondent No.1 filed objection, but the respondent No.2 has not filed objection statement.
6. The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 are as under:

The respondent No.1 contended in his written statement that driver of the Indica car bearing No.KA11A 4472 is having valid DL to drive the said car and was driving the same by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and driving the same very Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
2 slowly and following the rules and regulations.

The 2nd respondent never driven the vehicle with rash and negligent manner at any point of time by endangering to human life as alleged by the petitioner and accident caused only due to negligent manner of the deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna and its pillion riders.
The respondent No.1 is not liable to compensate any of the amount to the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
The accident has happened due to fault of the deceased only.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, abnormal and without any legal and equitable basis.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.
7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 16012018 at about 9.30 p.m. the deceased by name Santhosh @ Lakkanna was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA 04HB2586 and when he reached near Kanthaiahanapalya on Huliyurudurga - Amruturu Main Road, at that time, the driver of the Indica Car bearing reg.No.KA11A4472 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motorcycle, as a result, he sustained injuries and succumbed to the said injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that the accident has mainly occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Indica Car?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the only legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed?

if so, at what rate and from whom?
5. What order or award?
8. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents as ExP1 to 20.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 got examined as RW1 and produced his driving license as Ex.R.1.
9. Heard the arguments from the petitioners and respondent, petitioners filed written argument and the respondent has filed decision.
I have perused the records.

10. My finding to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the the Affirmative Issue No.4 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.5 : As per final order for the following:
Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
3 R E A S O N S 11. Issue No.1 and 2:
These issues are interconnected with each other.
Therefore both issues are taken for common discussion to avoid the repetition of facts.
12. The petitioners have filed present petition for compensation on the account of death of Santhosh @ Lakkanna in a road traffic accident took place on 16012018.
The claim petition is filed by the petitioners as they are the legal heirs of deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna and they are the father and mother of the deceased.

13. According to the petitioners, the deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA04HB2586 and he was returning to his native from Hemagiri Fair on Kanthaiahana palya to Amruthur Main road along with pillion riders
, at that time, the driver of the Indica Car bearing reg.No.KA11A4472 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased and pillion riders have sustained injury.
The deceased succumbed on the way to the hospital due to the accidental injury.
14. To substantiate the said fact, the petitioner No.1 got examined as Pw1 and produced documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.

The Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the PM report, Ex.P.4 is the inquest mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the charge sheet, Ex.P.6 is the IMV report, Ex.P.7 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.8 is the sketch, Ex.P.9 is the vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P.10 and 11 are the notice U/sec.133 of M.V.Act and Ex.P.12 and 13 are the replied to the police notice, Ex.P.14 is the photos with letter, Ex.P.15 is the certificate u/sec.65 (B), Ex.P.16 is the Form No.29, Ex.P.17 and 18 are the Notarized copy of Aadhar card and Ex.P.19 is the Ration Card and Ex.P.20 is the Genealogy tree.

15. On the other hand, the respondents contended that, the deceased and pillion riders were moving infront of them and deceased and pillion riders have fell down themselves from the motorcycle and at that time, the Car i.e., offending car came near to the spot of accident and they have helped to the deceased and other shifted to the hospital.
The offending car bearing reg.No.KA11A4472 was not at all involved in the accident.
The petitioners have falsely implicated the offending car.
To substantiate their defence, the respondent no.2 got examined as RW1 and produced his driving license as per Ex.R.1.

The RW1 in his evidence on affidavit stated that the rider of the motorcycle i.e., deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna coming from opposite direction with high speed along with 3 pillion riders in rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned to the right side and dashed against his car, due to which the rider and pillion riders fell down.
Further contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of rider of two wheeler, on humanity ground he stopped his car and helped the injured persons to shift the hospital.
The accident was not occurred on the negligence of the respondent No.2.
The petitioners and police have colluded with each and implicated the car in the case.

The RW1 has admitted the involvement of car in the accident, but in the written statement they have stated that the car has not at all involved in the accident and the same has been suggested to the PW1, but the same has been denied by the PW1.
After investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending car.
The The petitioners have produce the IMV report as per Ex.P.6, it disclose the damages to the both vehicles on front portion.
It shows that the accident was occurred as head on collusion.

The sketch as per ExP8 is discloses the road where Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
4 accident was occurred is straight road.
The PW1 clearly admitted that deceased had no DL and they were traveling four persons on motor cycle.
The respondent specifically alleged that the accident was occurred on the negligence of the deceased and he has contributed contributory negligence in the accident.
The petitioners counsel cross examined the RW1 but he has not taken any admission from the mouth of RW1 as there is no negligence on the deceased.

Though there is a charge sheet against the deceased for the offence punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 and 304A of IPC but itself is not sufficient to hold the accident solely on the negligence of driver of the offending car i.e., respondent No.2.
In this case there is no other evidence except police records and evidence of the PW1 and RW1.
The PW1 is not a eye witness and the RW1 eye witness to the accident and police sketch discloses the road where accident was occurred on the straight road.
Therefore, by considering all aspects, I am of the opinion that there is a contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence, I am of the opinion that the negligence of the deceased is 30% and negligence of the driver of the offending car is 70% in the accident.
Hence, I answer the above issue No. 1 and 2 partly in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.3:

The petitioners contended that they are the legal heirs of deceased Santhosh @
Lakkanna S/o Ramanna and they are depending upon the deceased.
The petitioners have produced their Aadhar card as per ExP17 and 18.
The petitioners have also produced the their ration card.
It discloses the name of the petitioners and deceased.
According to the petitioners they are the parents of deceased.
The respondents have not seriously disputed the relationship between deceased and petitioners.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence I answer issue No.3 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.4:

The specific contention of the petitioners is that, deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 25 years, working as a Waterman in Grampanchayat and also doing welding work and earning Rs.20,000/p.m.
Further the contention of the petitioners is that, due to unexpected death of Santhosh @ Lakkanna they have put to great hardship and lost their bread earner of the family.
18. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced the family ration card as per Ex P19.
The said ration card was issued in the year 2014 and at the time of issuance of ration card, the deceased age was 22 and the accident was occurred in the year 2018.
Therefore, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 26 years.

then the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '17'.
19.
Further to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced the documents.
Therefore, notional income has to be taken into consideration as per guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The notional income was fixed for the year 2018 as Rs.12,500/.

Therefore it is just and proper to take the salary of the deceased as of Rs.12,500/
p.m. and same is considered as income of the deceased as Rs.12,500/P.M.
20.

At this stage, I relied the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Pranay Sethi and others, has held at para No.61 as under:
Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
5

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(ii) .................
(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 4050 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 5060 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
21. In view of the above decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, I am of the view that, the deceased being aged below 26 years, an addition of 40% to the income should be added towards future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased Santhosh @ Lakkanna was aged about 26 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,500/p.m. (Rs.12,500 + 5,000 i.e.40%).
22. Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, on such deduction, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.8,750/p.m.
23.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8,750/ p.m. and the multiplier 17 is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.17,85,000/ (Rs.8,750 X 12 X 17)
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.17,85,000/ under the head of loss of dependency.

24. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/ each under the head of Filial consortium.

Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
6 25.

Further the petitioners are the father and mother of deceased and as such, in view of the Judgment of our Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (National Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Pranay Sethi) dated 31 102017,

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (National Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Pranay Sethi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/under the head of loss to the estate and also entitled for an amount of Rs.15,000/under the head of transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses.

26. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.18,95,000/ Under the following heads;
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs. 17,85,000/

2. Towards loss of filial Consortium Rs. 80,000/
3.

Towards loss to the estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 15,000/ body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses Total Rs. 18,95,000/
27.
LIABILITY:
On perusal of contents of petition, it appears that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending car bearing registration No.KA11/A4472 and respondent No.2 is the driver of the said car.
The respondents have disputed the sole negligence on the driver of the offending car and contended that there is a contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident.

The same has been established by the respondents and same is held as there is a contributory negligence of the deceased to the extent of 30% in the accident and 70% of the driver of the offending car while answering issue No.1 and 2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners as 70% in the total compensation amount.

For the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the respondents are liable to pay 70% in the total compensation of Rs.18,95,000/ with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.4 Partly in the affirmative.
28. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of above discussion on Point Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,95,000/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners as 70% in the total compensation amount and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

Sri.Ramanna vs Sri.Jairam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68899279/
7
Out of the above compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for 50% each of the compensation amount.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioners No.1 and 2, 40% each of the amount shall be kept in FD, in the name of petitioner No.1 and 2 in any nationalized/scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years and remaining amount with accrued interest shall be paid to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
